 Eagles make another trade, ship edge rusher to Bengals 
 The Eagles on Tuesday morning traded edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie to the Bengals. 
 By Dave Zangaro • 
 Published 45 minutes ago • 
 Updated 43 minutes ago 
 BOOKMARKER 
 Share 
 NBC Universal, Inc. 
 On this Emergency Eagle Eye podcast, Reuben Frank and Dave Zangaro react to the blockbuster trade. 
 The Jordan Davis trade wasn’t the end of Howie Roseman’s trade deadline haul.
 The Eagles on Tuesday morning agreed to trade edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie to the Cincinnati Bengals for a 2027 sixth-round pick, a league source confirmed to NBC Sports Philadelphia. 
 Before this trade, the Eagles did not have a sixth-round pick in the 2027 draft.
 Ebiketie, 27, joined the Eagles this offseason on a one-year deal and has played in all nine games this season. He has played a total of 300 snaps (48%) through this point in the season. That ranks third on the team at edge rusher behind Nolan Smith (359) and Jalyx Hunt (317).
 But now that Jonathan Greenard is healthier, he is expected to play more down the stretch. So the rotation for the rest of the 2026 season will include Smith, Hunt, Greenard, A.J. Epenesa and rookie Keyshawn James-Newby, who has been on the practice squad. Perhaps this will give James-Newby a chance to play more and develop; James-Newby has been elevated two times and has one more left. The Eagles also have Mason Reiger and Joshua Weru on the practice squad.
 Ebiketie this season has 25 tackles and 2 QB hits without a sack. He struggled against the run.
